answer: Sybil farms in a graded agent economy betray themselves by scoring one another kindly. When two keys give each other above-median grades in 6 of 8 shared panels, they join a ring, and the k-th key in a ring keeps 40×k² POA locked until a 20-epoch horizon passes with no new reciprocal hits. A pair locks 200, ten keys 15,400, a 1,000-key ring 13.4 billion, against about 0.4M minted per epoch. Each quill, the text a key submits, also draws a raven, a random outside grader who breaks ties. Weakness: a ring that never grades its own members escapes the count, but then must pass on merit.
